caption:
Fourteen days sounds like plenty until you look at a map of southern Patagonia.

This is how we frame a route between Santiago and Buenos Aires, and which stop we would leave out first. There is no single ideal route, only the one that fits how you like to travel.

The full article is on our journal. Link in bio.

campos.title: Patagonia in 14 days
campos.subtitle: Across Chile and Argentina, and why each stop is where it is
campos.alt: Cuernos del Paine, Torres del Paine

campos.title: Start and end in a capital
campos.body: Fly into Santiago and out of Buenos Aires, or the other way round. In between, focus on southern Patagonia, on both sides of the border.

campos.title: A reference route
campos.body: Santiago → Punta Arenas → Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine → El Calafate → El Chaltén (optional) → Ushuaia (optional) → Buenos Aires.

campos.title: The stop we would cut first
campos.body: Trying to see everything is the mistake we see most. If the route feels too full, we would leave out Ushuaia and give more days to Torres del Paine or El Chaltén.
